done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: `calendarYear` accepts a four-digit year only when the preceding text matches the narrow prefix list (or the question consists only of the year). Thus a follow-up such as “What were 2025 actuals?” is not recognized as naming 2025: the model window is cleared and the prior window is inherited. Conversely, “Show an amount of 2025” matches the allowed `of` prefix and has no recognized currency suffix, so it is incorrectly converted to calendar year 2025. These directly violate the Done-when requirements that a named year override prior/model windows and that an amount never be read as a year.
findings.title: Not done: Named-year follow-ups and unitless amounts still choose the wrong period

findings.body: The added coverage invokes `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, which replaces the provider, executor/database, audit, dimensions, and selection resolver with fakes (`backend/src/chat/chat.service.test.ts:979-1025`). The frontend Ask tests also mock the API (`frontend/src/features/assistant/ask-panel.test.tsx:33-42`), while `package.json:26` runs only Node/Vitest suites and the repository has no Playwright configuration, specification, or browser-test script. Therefore named-period follow-ups, prior-turn transport, no-period inheritance/aggregation, and period-control reruns remain unproven through the required browser, running API, and real database. The successful close run only executed the same lower-boundary tests.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
